mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, which leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises by >0.25% per month for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails when inflation exceeds 5% simultaneously.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% coincides with weakening household demand, which reduces corporate revenue growth and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the subsequent 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or GDP growth recovers above 1.5% within the next quarter.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate above 6.5% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profit margins, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes, or unemployment falls below 6% within the next month.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 1% for three consecutive months indicates contraction in manufacturing activity, which reduces earnings expectations and results in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls by >1% for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or industrial production rebounds by more than 2% in the following month.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both the federal funds rate and core CPI above their respective 12-month averages signals a dual tightening in monetary and inflationary conditions, which increases real discount rates and compresses equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL both exceed 12-month averages in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 45% of triggered episodes, or inflation falls below 2% within the next quarter.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in the Housing Starts index (HOUST) above its 12-month moving average by more than 10% indicates a robust housing recovery, which boosts construction-related equities and supports broader market gains, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or housing starts decline by more than 5% in the following month.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in both payroll employment (PAYEMS) and unemployment rate (UNRATE) over a two-month period signals a paradoxical labor market where job creation is insufficient to lower unemployment, often preceding a slowdown, which predicts negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases while UNRATE also increases over two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of triggered episodes, or unemployment falls by more than 1 percentage point within the next quarter.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in real retail sales (RSAFS) below its 6-month moving average for four consecutive months signals weakening consumer demand, which reduces revenue growth for consumer-facing sectors and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS < 6-month moving average for 4 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or real retail sales rebound above the 6-month moving average within two months.
